Flatten an Rd text fragment into a single string, with inline Markdown

Source: R/utils.R
dot-rd_to_text.Rd

Rd fragments are themselves nested lists of text and tag nodes (e.g. for \\code{} or \\link{}). .rd_to_text() recursively reduces a fragment to a single-line-safe string, normalizing horizontal whitespace, and renders common inline Rd tags as their Markdown equivalent (\\code{} -> `x`, \\emph{} -> _x_, \\href{}{} -> [text](url), etc. - see .rd_inline_piece()) rather than silently stripping them to plain text.

Usage

.rd_to_text(rd, in_code = FALSE)

Arguments

rd

An Rd fragment or a list of Rd fragments.

in_code

Whether this call is already nested inside a code-styled wrapper (\\code{}/\\command{}/\\link{}). Threaded through recursion so that e.g. \\code{\link{x}} (an extremely common pattern) renders as a single `x` instead of doubly-wrapped x - each nested code-styled tag only adds backticks when it isn't already inside one.

Value

A single, trimmed string.

Details

Some Rd macros (e.g. \\I{}) are parsed into a leaf node tagged "USERMACRO" whose value is a character vector like c("#1", "bar") - a #N placeholder token followed by the actual substituted text, rather than a plain scalar. Placeholder tokens are dropped so the substituted text is used (see .leaf_rd_text()).

This is "Tier 2" of csdocs's text extraction (single-line inline). Use .rd_to_raw_text() ("Tier 1") instead for code content (\\usage{}/\\examples{}/\\preformatted{}) where exact whitespace must survive, and .rd_to_block_md() ("Tier 3", in render_rd_block.R) for rich multi-paragraph content (\\description{}/\\details{}) that may contain lists, subsections, or code blocks.
